concurrent parallel test runs fail on the shared compiled view directory laravel version 13.34.0 (also present on 13.x at d6e9b9a7d8) php version 8.4.20 database driver & version no response description illuminate\testing\concerns\testviews gives each parallel worker its own compiled view directory by appending paralleltesting::token(). the token is the worker index, 1 to n, so it is the same in every parallel run. it isolates workers within a run, but two parallel runs of the same project at the same time use the same test 1, test 2, ... directories. both process callbacks that manage that directory fail when another run touches it at the same moment: php paralleltesting::setupprocess(fn () => file::ensuredirectoryexists($path)); paralleltesting::teardownprocess(fn () => file::deletedirectory($path)); - ensuredirectoryexists() checks isdirectory() and then calls makedirectory() without $force, so it reaches the unsuppressed mkdir(). if the other run creates the directory in between, this run fails with mkdir(): file exists. - deletedirectory() checks isdirectory() and then constructs a filesystemiterator, which throws unexpectedvalueexception if the other run removed the directory in between. either way, the losing run fails before or after its tests, although nothing in the tests is wrong. it shows up when two parallel runs share a checkout, for example a developer's run beside a local ci job, or two terminals. the trace from the losing run: mkdir(): file exists at illuminate/filesystem/filesystem.php:662 illuminate\filesystem\filesystem->makedirectory() at filesystem.php:643 illuminate\filesystem\filesystem->ensuredirectoryexists() at facade.php:364 illuminate\support\facades\facade:: callstatic() at testing/concerns/testviews.php:26 steps to reproduce in any application with a parallel-capable test suite, start two parallel runs in the same directory at the same time: bash php artisan test --parallel & php artisan test --parallel & wait it is timing-dependent, so it may take a few attempts. the window is widest with many workers and a short suite. the deterministic version is the test added in 61786, which forces each check to see the state from just before the other run acted.

with in eloquent/builder fails when passing callback as null instead of calling it with only relations. laravel version 12 and 13 php version 8.4 database driver & version no response description when calling $builder->with($relations, null) explicitly func get args() incorrectly interprets null as 0 if $relations is a string. we had this because we extended the builder and had a with($relations, $callback = null) signature ourselves which called parent::with($relations, $callback), thus passing the null generated from our own default, instead of letting the parent generate its null default. steps to reproduce call any builder::with() method with a string in relations and null passed explicitly to callback instead of defaulting to null.

cloudbootstrapper renumbers pgsql pdo options for -pooler hosts (array merge on int keys) laravel version 13.31.0 (same code on the current 13.x branch) php version 8.4.25 database driver & version pgsql, laravel cloud serverless postgres through the -pooler endpoint description when database.connections.pgsql.host contains pg.laravel.cloud and -pooler, cloudbootstrapper::configureunpooledpostgresconnection() adds emulated prepares like this: php $app['config']->set( 'database.connections.pgsql.options', array merge( $app['config']->get('database.connections.pgsql.options', []), [pdo::attr emulate prepares => true], ), ); pdo attribute keys are integers, and array merge() renumbers integer keys. any pdo options the app already set are therefore re-keyed from 0 and applied to the wrong attributes. for example: php array merge( [pdo::attr timeout => 5, pdo::attr persistent => true, pdo\pgsql::attr disable prepares => true], [pdo::attr emulate prepares => true], ); // [0 => 5, 1 => true, 2 => true, 3 => true] // = attr autocommit => 5, attr prefetch => true, attr timeout => 1, attr errmode => 1 (errmode warning) effects: - attr emulate prepares itself is lost. so is any attr persistent or pdo\pgsql::attr disable prepares the app set. - attr errmode becomes errmode warning. the key 3 value overrides the connector's default errmode exception, so query errors surface as php warnings (errorexception) instead of queryexception. - the connect timeout becomes 1 second. because emulation is lost, pdo pgsql uses named server-side prepared statements through the transaction pooler. with a libpq older than 17, pdo pgsql frees statements with sql deallocate pdo stmt n. pgbouncer (max prepared statements > 0) has renamed the statements to pgbouncer n, so the deallocate fails with 26000. pdo pgsql ignores that error, but the open transaction is aborted, and the next statement fails: sqlstate[25p02]: in failed sql transaction: error: current transaction is aborted, commands ignored until end of transaction block we hit this in db::transaction() blocks with more than one query (a deploy seeder) right after switching db host to the -pooler endpoint. the default config/database.php sets no pgsql options, so apps on the stock config are not affected. any app that sets pdo options on pgsql is. steps to reproduce php config([ 'database.connections.pgsql.host' => 'ep-example-123456-pooler.us-east-2.pg.laravel.cloud', 'database.connections.pgsql.options' => [ pdo::attr timeout => 5, pdo::attr persistent => true, ], ]); \illuminate\foundation\cloudbootstrapper::configureunpooledpostgresconnection(app()); var dump(config('database.connections.pgsql.options')); // array(3) { [0]=> int(5) [1]=> bool(true) [2]=> bool(true) } // expected: [pdo::attr timeout => 5, pdo::attr persistent => true, pdo::attr emulate prepares => true] end to end: a laravel cloud app whose pgsql connection sets any pdo options, db host pointed at the -pooler endpoint, and a db::transaction() that runs two queries. it fails with 25p02 on the second query. suggested fix: assign the key instead of merging, for example $app['config']->set('database.connections.pgsql.options.'.pdo::attr emulate prepares, true), so existing integer keys are preserved and emulation is forced as intended.

proxy trust granted on missing trustedproxy.proxies configuration file laravel version 12.22.0, 13.0.0 php version 8.4 database driver & version no response description illuminate\http\middleware\trustproxies ships in laravel's default global middleware stack and decides whether the application should honour x-forwarded- headers. that decision is a trust boundary: forwarding headers are only meaningful once the request has been shown to originate from a known reverse proxy, which is normally established by matching remote addr — the one request property an attacker cannot forge — against an operator-configured proxy list. when no trusted proxies have been configured, the middleware attempts to auto-detect laravel's own hosting platforms and, on a match, trusts every proxy. of the three auto-detection conditions, only laravel cloud() reads server-side state; the other two key on the request's host header: php $trustedips = $this->proxies() ?: config('trustedproxy.proxies'); // :69 if (is null($trustedips) && (laravel cloud() || // :72 server-side str ends with($request->host(), '.on-forge.com') || // :73 client-controlled str ends with($request->host(), '.on-vapor.com'))) { // :74 client-controlled $trustedips = ' '; // :75 } handle() clears the trusted-proxy list at line 54 before this check runs. request::host() delegates to symfony's gethost(), which substitutes x-forwarded-host only when the request already arrives from a trusted proxy; with the list empty that condition is false by construction, so $request->host() returns the raw client-supplied host header. the security decision is therefore taken on attacker-controlled input, and on a match the trusted-proxy list is set to 0.0.0.0/0 and ::/0 at line 122 — every host on the internet. nothing in a default installation prevents the attacker from supplying that host value. the trusthosts middleware, which would reject unrecognised hosts, is excluded from the stack by protected $trusthosts = false in foundation/configuration/middleware.php:105, and the documentation states that laravel responds to all requests regardless of host by default. no trustedproxy.php configuration file ships with the framework, so the config('trustedproxy.proxies') fallback at line 69 resolves to null and the auto-detection branch is reached. suggested remediation remove the two str ends with($request->host(), ...) clauses at lines 73-74. platform auto-detection must derive from server-side state, exactly as the adjacent laravel cloud() call already does by reading $ env['laravel cloud'] / $ server['laravel cloud'] (support/helpers.php:233-237). forge and vapor should expose an equivalent provisioning-time environment variable, and the branch should key on that: php if (is null($trustedips) && (laravel cloud() || laravel forge() || laravel vapor())) { $trustedips = ' '; } additionally, the documentation for trusted proxies does not describe it as a security control, while the config('trustedproxy.proxies') fallback read at line 69 is not documented at all. framing trusted-proxy configuration as a trust-boundary decision would make the consequences of leaving it unset visible to operators. steps to reproduce 1. create an empty working directory containing a single composer.json: json { "require": { "laravel/framework": "^13.0" } } 2. install the dependencies: composer install 3. create poc.php alongside it with the following content. each request is built with a fixed, honest remote addr of 198.51.100.7 and a forged x-forwarded-for: 1.2.3.4; only the host: header varies: php instance('config', new repository([])); container::setinstance($container); function probe(string $host): void { request::settrustedproxies([], request::header x forwarded for); $request = request::create(' 'get', [], [], [], [ 'remote addr' => '198.51.100.7', // the real client socket 'http host' => $host, 'http x forwarded for' => '1.2.3.4', // forged by the client 'http x forwarded proto' => 'https', // forged by the client ]); (new trustproxies)->handle($request, fn ($r) => $r); printf("host: %-18s trustedproxies=%-26s ip()=%-14s secure()=%s\n", $host, json encode(request::gettrustedproxies()), $request->ip(), $request->secure() ? 'true' : 'false' ); } probe('app.example'); // control: ordinary host probe('pwn.on-forge.com'); // attacker-chosen suffix probe('x.on-vapor.com'); // attacker-chosen suffix 4. run it: php poc.php 5. observe that the client-supplied host: header alone decides whether the forged x-forwarded-for is honoured: host: app.example trustedproxies=[] ip()=198.51.100.7 secure()=false host: pwn.on-forge.com trustedproxies=["0.0.0.0\/0","::\/0"] ip()=1.2.3.4 secure()=true host: x.on-vapor.com trustedproxies=["0.0.0.0\/0","::\/0"] ip()=1.2.3.4 secure()=true the first line is the control: with an ordinary host:, no proxies are trusted and ip() correctly returns the real remote addr. on lines two and three the request is byte-for-byte identical apart from the host: value, yet the trusted-proxy list has become 0.0.0.0/0 + ::/0, ip() now returns the attacker-chosen 1.2.3.4, and secure() has been spoofed to true via x-forwarded-proto. no server-side state was changed between the three calls — laravel cloud() is false throughout, and $proxies is unset.

missing guard in dominantcolor() and dimensions() laravel version 13.32.0 php version 8.4.21 database driver & version no response description summary interventiondriver::process() runs a default-deny mime allowlist immediately before manager->decode(). the sibling public methods dominantcolor() and dimensions() call the same manager->decode() with no such check, and image::dominantcolor() feeds them the raw upload bytes when no transform is queued. so the framework applies its own pre-decode input allowlist inconsistently across methods that perform the identical decode — an unvalidated upload reaches the decoder through the unguarded paths. details all three methods in interventiondriver reach the same manager->decode($contents), but only process() guards it (src/illuminate/image/drivers/interventiondriver.php): php public function process(string $contents, imagepipeline $pipeline): string { $mimetype = (new finfo(fileinfo mime type))->buffer($contents); if (! in array($mimetype, ['image/jpeg', 'image/png', 'image/bmp', 'image/gif', 'image/webp', 'image/avif', 'image/x-avif', 'image/heic', 'image/x-heic', 'image/heif'])) { throw new imageexception("the image format [{$mimetype}] is not supported."); // guard } $image = $this->manager->decode($contents); // ... } public function dimensions(string $contents): array { $image = $this->manager->decode($contents); // no guard // ... } public function dominantcolor(string $contents): string { $image = $this->manager->decode($contents); // no guard // ... } image::dominantcolor() feeds this the raw upload bytes when no transform is queued (it only routes through process() on haschanges()), and request::image() builds the image with zero pre-validation. impact - default configuration (image driver=gd, or imagick with a stock modern policy.xml): no security impact. gd cannot decode the hostile vector/document formats and simply errors; a default imagick policy.xml already disables the dangerous coders. the unvalidated bytes reach the decoder, but the decode fails harmlessly (a 500). the unconditional, framework-owned defect is the guard inconsistency itself. steps to reproduce 1. setup a test app: bash composer create-project laravel/laravel img001 && cd img001 composer require laravel/framework:13.32.0 intervention/image:^4.0 2. create the file poc.php — the guarded transform vs. the unguarded accent-color read, each surfacing the exception class: php make(illuminate\contracts\console\kernel::class)->bootstrap(); // truncated tiff: finfo => image/tiff (outside process()'s allowlist), and its // binary magic routes intervention to the blob decoder (readimageblob on imagick). $payload = "ii \x00\x08\x00\x00\x00"; // process() has the finfo allowlist -> rejects before decoding: try { (new image(fn () => $payload))->cover(64, 64)->tobytes(); } catch (throwable $e) { echo 'process() => '.$e::class.' : '.$e->getmessage().php eol; } // dominantcolor() has no allowlist -> bytes reach the decoder: try { (new image(fn () => $payload))->dominantcolor(); } catch (throwable $e) { echo 'dominantcolor() => '.$e::class.' : '.$e->getmessage().php eol; } 3. run the poc and notice the different behaviours: process() => illuminate\image\imageexception : the image format [image/tiff] is not supported. dominantcolor() => intervention\image\exceptions\imagedecoderexception : failed to decode unsupported image format from binary data

databasetruncation combined with a transactional base testcase silently runs migrate:fresh on every test and never truncates laravel version: 13.32.0 php version: 8.3.33 database driver & version: mysql 8.0.30 --- description when a base testcase uses refreshdatabase (or lazilyrefreshdatabase) and an individual test class uses databasetruncation, both strategies are applied. two things then go wrong: - the schema is rebuilt from scratch on every test — twice per test, in fact. - the tables are never truncated at all. truncatetablesforallconnections() is never reached; isolation comes incidentally from the migrate:fresh that replaces it. on a clean laravel 13.32.0 app with 43 migrations, a 3-test class issued 294 create table and 0 truncate statements, against an expected 49 and 2. the tests still pass, so nothing signals that anything is wrong. the only visible symptom is the suite getting dramatically slower. why both traits get applied setuptraits() resolves strategies with class uses recursive(static::class), which does not distinguish a trait used directly by the test class from one inherited via the base class. the four strategies are then dispatched as independent if blocks with no mutual exclusion: php if (isset($uses[refreshdatabase::class])) { $this->refreshdatabase(); } if (isset($uses[databasemigrations::class])) { $this->rundatabasemigrations(); } if (isset($uses[databasetruncation::class])) { $this->truncatedatabasetables(); } if (isset($uses[databasetransactions::class])) { $this->begindatabasetransaction(); } so a class that inherits lazilyrefreshdatabase and adds databasetruncation gets both, with no error or warning. why that produces a rebuild per test refreshdatabase::begindatabasetransaction() registers a teardown that invalidates the migrated state if the connection is no longer inside the transaction it opened: php if ($connection->getpdo() && ! $connection->getpdo()->intransaction()) { refreshdatabasestate::$migrated = false; } in isolation this is correct and deliberate — a test that committed has escaped the rollback guarantee, so rebuilding is the safe recovery. but databasetruncation commits by design ; that is its entire purpose. so the condition is true after every test, and $migrated is reset every time. databasetruncation::truncatedatabasetables() then re-enters its first-run branch on every subsequent test: php if (! refreshdatabasestate::$migrated) { $this->artisan('migrate:fresh', $this->migratefreshusing()); $this->app[kernel::class]->setartisan(null); refreshdatabasestate::$migrated = true; return; // insert(['name' => 'x']); $this->assertsame(1, db::table('pad 001')->count()); } public function test one(): void { $this->touchdatabase(); } public function test two(): void { $this->touchdatabase(); } public function test three(): void { $this->touchdatabase(); } } 3. drop and recreate the test schema, then run the class while watching mysql's own counters: sql show global status like 'com create table'; show global status like 'com truncate'; expected: one migrate:fresh on the first test (49 create table), then a truncation pass before each subsequent test (2 truncate batches). actual: six full schema rebuilds and no truncation at all. measurement identical 3 tests, same app, same machine: | setup | create table | truncate | wall | |---|---|---|---| | lazilyrefreshdatabase base + databasetruncation | 294 (6 rebuilds) | 0 | 3808ms | | same, with refreshdatabase() overridden to a no-op | 49 (1 rebuild) | 2 | 930ms | the tests pass in both cases. note the count: 294 = 3 tests x 2 rebuilds x 49 tables. there appear to be two rebuilds per test, because truncatedatabasetables() invokes artisan('migrate:fresh'), whose query activity trips lazilyrefreshdatabase's beforeexecuting hook mid-flight and nests a second migratedatabases() inside the first. begindatabasetransaction() then registers its teardown, which finds the connection outside a transaction (the ddl having implicitly committed), resets $migrated, and the cycle repeats on the next test. because $migrated is false on entry to every test, truncatedatabasetables() always takes the early-return branch, which is why truncatetablesforallconnections() is never reached and com truncate stays at zero. for scale, on a real application (112 migrations, 87 tests across 6 classes) the same collision cost roughly 9x: one 6-test class took 36.1s instead of 4.1s. possible directions i'm happy to open a pr, but the right approach isn't obvious to me and i'd rather ask than guess: 1. throw when more than one strategy resolves in setuptraits(). clearest signal, and everything needed is already in scope at that point — but it would break any application currently combining traits, so presumably it could only be considered for a major release. 2. give one strategy precedence — e.g. skip refreshdatabase() when databasetruncation is present. non-erroring and strictly faster, but it does change behaviour for existing combined setups. 3. stop the teardown reset clobbering truncation's state. closest to root cause. refreshdatabasestate::$migrated is documented as "indicates if the test database has been migrated", which is a legitimately shared concern; the issue is that a refreshdatabase-specific recovery path writes to it. i'd want to understand the original motivation for that reset before narrowing it, so as not to reintroduce whatever it was guarding against. happy to implement whichever of these you'd accept, or something else entirely. workaround for anyone who lands here from a search: override refreshdatabase() to a no-op in the truncating test class, so no transaction is ever opened. a trait used directly by the class takes precedence over the method inherited from the parent, so this suppresses the transactional strategy while leaving truncation intact. ---

appendtoprioritylist() appends to the end of the list when the referenced middleware is first laravel version 13.31.0 php version 8.4.25 database driver & version no response description adding middleware after another entry in the priority list puts it at the end of the list instead, but only when the referenced middleware is the first entry. php ->withmiddleware(function (middleware $middleware) { $middleware->appendtoprioritylist( handleprecognitiverequests::class, // the first entry of the default priority list ensuretenantisset::class, ); }) ensuretenantisset ends up last in the priority list rather than second, so it runs after authentication, throttling and session handling instead of right after the entry it was placed behind. kernel::addtomiddlewarepriorityrelative() starts the insertion point at 0 and only moves it when the match sits further along: php $index = $after ? 0 : count($this->middlewarepriority); foreach ((array) $existing as $existingmiddleware) { if (in array($existingmiddleware, $this->middlewarepriority)) { $middlewareindex = array search($existingmiddleware, $this->middlewarepriority); if ($after && $middlewareindex > $index) { $index = $middlewareindex + 1; } elseif ($after === false && $middlewareindex middlewarepriority, $middleware); } elseif (($after && $index === 0) || $index === count($this->middlewarepriority)) { $this->middlewarepriority[] = $middleware; } else { array splice($this->middlewarepriority, $index, 0, $middleware); } for a match at position 0 the guard is 0 > 0, which is false, so $index stays at its initial value. the branch below then reads $after && $index === 0 as "the referenced middleware was not found" and appends. 0 is serving both as the starting value and as a real position, and the two cases are indistinguishable by the time the branch runs. starting from [a, b, c, d]: | call | expected | actual | | --- | --- | --- | | addtomiddlewarepriorityafter('a', 'x') | a, x, b, c, d | a, b, c, d, x | | addtomiddlewarepriorityafter('b', 'x') | a, b, x, c, d | a, b, x, c, d | | addtomiddlewarepriorityafter('d', 'x') | a, b, c, d, x | a, b, c, d, x | | addtomiddlewarepriorityafter(['a', 'missing'], 'x') | a, x, b, c, d | a, b, c, d, x | | addtomiddlewareprioritybefore('a', 'x') | x, a, b, c, d | x, a, b, c, d | | addtomiddlewareprioritybefore('d', 'x') | a, b, c, x, d | a, b, c, x, d | only "after the first entry" is affected. every other position is placed correctly, and addtomiddlewareprioritybefore() is correct throughout, including for the first entry, because its starting value is count($this->middlewarepriority) rather than a reachable position. there is no error or warning; the middleware is registered, just in a different place than asked for. steps to reproduce composer require laravel/framework php middlewarepriority = $priority; } public function priority(): array { return $this->middlewarepriority; } } $first = new probekernel; $first->setpriority(['a', 'b', 'c']); $first->addtomiddlewarepriorityafter('a', 'x'); $second = new probekernel; $second->setpriority(['a', 'b', 'c']); $second->addtomiddlewarepriorityafter('b', 'x'); var dump($first->priority(), $second->priority()); expected: ['a', 'x', 'b', 'c'] and ['a', 'b', 'x', 'c']. actual: ['a', 'b', 'c', 'x'] and ['a', 'b', 'x', 'c']. the subclass only exists to keep the reproduction short — it skips the constructor and the router sync, and does not touch the method under test. the same happens through appendtoprioritylist() in bootstrap/app.php, which reaches addtomiddlewarepriorityafter() via applicationbuilder.

exception log level configured with level() is ignored when a broader type was registered first laravel version 13.31.0 php version 8.4.25 database driver & version no response description the log level chosen for an exception depends on the order in which level() was called, not on how specific the matching type is. when a broader type is registered first, the level configured for a more specific type is silently ignored. php ->withexceptions(function (exceptions $exceptions) { $exceptions->level(exception::class, loglevel::warning); $exceptions->level(pdoexception::class, loglevel::critical); }) a pdoexception is logged as warning. swapping the two lines logs it as critical. handler::maploglevel() picks the first entry that matches: php return arr::first( $this->levels, fn ($level, $type) => $e instanceof $type, loglevel::error ); $levels is keyed by registration order, and arr::first() stops at the first match, so exception::class wins for every exception once it is registered, regardless of what is registered afterwards. $levels starts empty, so nothing in the framework causes this — only the order of the calls. there is no error or warning; the exception is still reported, just at the other level. a database outage logged as warning instead of critical will not raise whatever the critical level is wired to. the surrounding configuration in the same handler does not behave this way. dontreport(), reportable() and renderable() all match on "any registered type matches", so their registration order does not change the outcome. level() is the one where it silently does. steps to reproduce composer require laravel/framework php levels[] = $level; } }; $container = new container; $container->instance(loggerinterface::class, $spy); // broader type registered first. $handler = new handler($container); $handler->level(exception::class, loglevel::warning); $handler->level(pdoexception::class, loglevel::critical); $handler->report(new pdoexception('db down')); // same configuration, lines swapped. $other = new handler($container); $other->level(pdoexception::class, loglevel::critical); $other->level(exception::class, loglevel::warning); $other->report(new pdoexception('db down')); var dump($spy->levels); expected: ['critical', 'critical'] — pdoexception::class is the more specific of the two registered types in both cases. actual: ['warning', 'critical'].

typeerror in sessionguard::userfromrecaller() when getauthpassword() is null (passwordless apps) laravel version: 13.31.0 (12.x is affected identically — see history) php version: 8.5.4 database driver & version: mysql 8.4.11 description sessionguard::userfromrecaller() throws a typeerror — a 500 on every request — when the user matched by the remember-me cookie has a null auth password: typeerror: hash equals(): argument 1 ($known string) must be of type string, null given at vendor/laravel/framework/src/illuminate/auth/sessionguard.php:239 0 sessionguard.php(239): hash equals() 1 sessionguard.php(197): illuminate\auth\sessionguard->userfromrecaller() 2 authmanager.php(61): illuminate\auth\sessionguard->user() 3 authserviceprovider.php(89): call user func() 4 request.php(677): call user func() the code, identical in 12.x and 13.x: php $userpassword = $user->getauthpassword(); $recallerhash = $recaller->hash(); return (hash equals($this->hashpasswordforcookie($userpassword), $recallerhash) || hash equals($userpassword, $recallerhash)) ? $user : null; we run a passwordless application — login is otp and passkey only, and the users table has no password column at all — so getauthpassword() returns null for every user. after upgrading from 13.26.1 to 13.30.1, every user holding a remember-me cookie got a 500 on their first request once the session expired: home page, login page, every route. it keeps happening on each request until the cookie expires or the user clears it, and since the crash happens while resolving the user, there is no logout path to recover from it in the browser. two separate things go wrong: 1. hashpasswordforcookie(null) calls hash hmac('sha256', null, ...), which raises deprecated: hash hmac(): passing null to parameter 2 ($data) of type string is deprecated and returns the hmac of the empty string. so the first comparison silently compares against the wrong value. 2. the second hash equals($userpassword, $recallerhash) then gets the raw null and throws. cookies issued before 61386 store the auth password itself as the third segment, which for these users is an empty string. recaller::hasallsegments() only requires the first two segments to be non-empty, so such a cookie passes valid() and reaches the comparison. worth noting that the deprecation in (1) also fires on the write path: queuerecallercookie() calls hashpasswordforcookie($user->getauthpassword()), so the framework itself feeds a null to hash hmac() when issuing the cookie. under php 9 that stops being a deprecation. why this reads as a bug rather than a misconfiguration a null auth password is treated as a supported state everywhere else in the same component: - eloquentuserprovider::validatecredentials() — if (is null($hashed = $user->getauthpassword())) { return false; } - databaseuserprovider::validatecredentials() — identical guard - illuminate\session\middleware\authenticatesession::handle() — if (! $request->hassession() || ! $request->user() || ! $request->user()->getauthpassword()) { return $next($request); } userfromrecaller() is now the only place in the auth stack that assumes a string. history - 61386 added the password-hash check to userfromrecaller() in 12.x. - 61396 reported a typeerror on the no matching user path; fixed by 61397 with if (! $this->viaremember) { return; }. that guard is present in 13.30.1+. - 61433 proposed the fix for this no password path and was closed without comment on 2026-09-04. both 12.x and 13.x still carry the unguarded code as of today, and the change reached 13.x through commit 3005430 ("port fixes from 12.x"), released in v13.30.1 — which is not mentioned in that release's notes, so there was nothing to react to at upgrade time. what i am actually asking if a null getauthpassword() is no longer supported, that is a perfectly reasonable answer — but then it is a behavioural break that deserves a line in the upgrade guide, and the three null-guards listed above are dead code that suggests the opposite. if it is still supported, userfromrecaller() needs the guard that authenticatesession already has. either way, an application should not be able to 500 itself on every route with a cookie the framework issued. steps to reproduce on a fresh application: 1. make users.password nullable, or remove the column so getauthpassword() returns null. 2. while on 13.29.0 (or 12.68), call auth::login($user, remember: true). equivalently, hand-craft the cookie value as {id}|{remember token}| — an empty third segment is what these users get. 3. upgrade to 13.30.1 or later (12.69 or later on 12.x). 4. delete the session cookie, keep remember web , and request any route that resolves the user. every request returns 500 until the cookie is gone. on 13.29.0 the same cookie logs the user in. workaround for anyone who lands here from a search, on the application side: php // app/models/user.php public function getauthpassword(): string { return ''; } existing cookies keep working — the empty third segment matches on the second comparison, new ones match on the first — and authenticatesession still skips its check. the remember token itself is still verified by retrievebytoken(), so a forged cookie still resolves to a guest.

lazycollection::take() returns wrong items for a negative limit larger than the collection laravel version 13.31.0 php version 8.4.25 database driver & version no response description take() with a negative limit returns the last $limit items. when the collection holds fewer items than the limit, collection returns the whole collection, but lazycollection returns a null entry, drops real items, and emits warnings from inside the framework. php (new collection(['a', 'b', 'c']))->take(-5)->all(); // ['a', 'b', 'c'] (new lazycollection(['a', 'b', 'c']))->take(-5)->all(); // ['' => null, 0 => 'a'] warning: undefined array key 3 in .../illuminate/collections/lazycollection.php on line 1577 warning: trying to access array offset on null in .../illuminate/collections/lazycollection.php on line 1577 the two classes implement the same enumerable contract, so swapping one for the other silently changes the result here. this only happens when abs($limit) is greater than the number of items. every combination where abs($limit) null] | | 2 | -3 | ['a', 'b'] | ['' => null, 0 => 'a'] | | 3 | -5 | ['a', 'b', 'c'] | ['' => null, 0 => 'a'] | | 4 | -5 | ['a', 'b', 'c', 'd'] | ['' => null, 0 => 'a', 1 => 'b', 2 => 'c'] | | 5 | -7 | ['a', 'b', 'c', 'd', 'e'] | ['' => null, 0 => 'a', 1 => 'b', 2 => 'c'] | steps to reproduce composer require illuminate/collections php take(-5)->all()); var dump((new lazycollection(['a', 'b', 'c']))->take(-5)->all()); expected: both return ['a', 'b', 'c']. actual: the lazycollection call emits four warnings and returns ['' => null, 0 => 'a']. a fix was proposed in 61489.

contains/doesnt contain validation rules use inconsistent comparison strictness laravel version 13.30.1 php version 8.3.33 database driver & version mysql 8.0 (issue is related to validation logic, no db involved) description while validating a field with both contains and doesnt contain rules, we expect them to always be logical opposites.. that means, a value either contains a given item or it doesn't, never can be both. instead, for certain loosely-typed array values, both rules pass at the same time on identical input, which shouldn't be possible. the cause here is - validatecontains and validatedoesntcontain use inconsistent comparison strictness.. both live in validatecontains() (validatesattributes.php and validatedoesntcontain() (validatesattributes.php: php public function validatecontains($attribute, $value, $parameters) { if (! is array($value)) { return false; } return array all($parameters, fn ($parameter) => in array($parameter, $value)); // here is the loose comparison } public function validatedoesntcontain($attribute, $value, $parameters) { if (! is array($value)) { return false; } return array all($parameters, fn ($parameter) => ! in array($parameter, $value, true)); // here is the strict comparison } contains uses a loose in array(), while doesnt contain uses a strict in array(..., true). so as they don't share the same comparison logic, a value like true in the array and a rule parameter like "1" can satisfy both rules at the same time: loosely, "1" == true is true, so contains:1 passes; whereas strictly, "1" !== true is also true, so doesnt contain:1 also passes! i checked at the git history regarding this and found that the two rules were briefly aligned before. pr 61318 made doesnt contain strict specifically to close numeric-string loose-comparison collision.. and a companion pr ( 61320) made contains strict too, which would have kept the two rules consistent, but it was reverted later ( 61330). per the discussion on 61320, @crynobone flagged that the strict change may cause a breaking change, because rule parameters (contains:1) always arrive as strings, while array values can be int/bool/float, so strict comparison against a string parameter stops matching non-string values.. it's the same class of issue that in rule's fix ( 61146) had already solved by casting the value to string before comparing strictly. but contains never got that string-casting fix, so its strict attempt was reverted outright and it has remained loose since then.. steps to reproduce php use illuminate\support\facades\validator; $data = ['flags' => [true]]; $contains = validator::make($data, ['flags' => 'contains:1'])->passes(); $doesntcontain = validator::make($data, ['flags' => 'doesnt contain:1'])->passes(); var dump($contains); // true - "1" loosely equals true here var dump($doesntcontain); // true - "1" is not strictly equals true // this is the contradiction: a value can't both contain and not contain the "same" item // expected: exactly one of these should pass.

redis tagged cache fails to invalidate touched entries after flushstale() laravel version 13.x php version 8.4 / 8.5 database driver & version redis (phpredis or predis) description when calling touch() on a redis tagged cache entry, the redis key's ttl is successfully extended in redis, but its expiration score in the tag's underlying sorted set (tag:{name}:entries) remains unchanged with the original timestamp. problem & impact: if a scheduled or background cleanup task runs flushstale() after the item's original ttl has passed: 1. flushstale() removes the item from the tag's sorted set because its score is in the past. 2. however, the item itself is still active in redis because its ttl was extended by touch(). 3. when the application subsequently invalidates the tag using tags(['...'])->flush(), laravel reads the tag's sorted set to determine which keys to delete (del). since the key was prematurely purged from the sorted set, it is not deleted by the tag flush (it remains in redis until its touched ttl expires). 4. a subsequent tags(['...'])->get($key) continues to return the stale cached data instead of null. this causes silent cache invalidation failures and data inconsistencies in production systems that extend ttls via touch() and periodically clean stale references with flushstale(). for context, i previously submitted 61467 with a proposed fix and regression tests; that pr was closed. could you clarify whether the behavior described here is expected for tagged cache entries after touch()? steps to reproduce the following reproduction uses pest in a bootstrapped laravel application configured with a redis cache store: php use illuminate\support\carbon; use illuminate\support\facades\cache; it('reproduces redis tagged cache desync after touch and flushstale', function () { carbon::settestnow($now = carbon::create(2026, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0)); try { $cache = cache::store('redis')->tags(['orders']); // 1. store item for 60 seconds $cache->put('order:100', 'active order', 60); // 2. extend ttl to 120 seconds using touch() $cache->touch('order:100', 120); // 3. move time forward past original ttl (61 seconds) carbon::settestnow($now->copy()->addseconds(61)); // 4. stale cleanup runs $cache->flushstale(); // key is still active in redis (as expected with 120s ttl) expect($cache->get('order:100'))->tobe('active order'); // 5. invalidate tag $cache->flush(); // 6. failure: expect null since tag was flushed, but returns 'active order' expect($cache->get('order:100'))->tobenull(); } finally { carbon::settestnow(); } }); expected behavior: flushing a tag must invalidate all active items under that tag, even if their expiration was extended using touch(). actual behavior: the assertion fails with: failed asserting that 'active order' is null.

wherepivot() closure scope is ignored by detach(), updateexistingpivot(), and sync(), which causes unscoped pivot deletes laravel version 13.30.1 php version 8.3.33 database driver & version mysql 8.0 (issue is driver-agnostic) description i have a belongstomany relation scoped with the new closure form of wherepivot() (added in 61150), and i used detach() to remove only the pivot rows matching that specific scope. instead, detach() removes all pivot rows for the parent model.. ignoring the closure scope i defined. digging into it, found that wherepivot() handles the closure and string forms differently (belongstomany.php { if ($column instanceof closure) { $pivotquery = (new ($this->getpivotclass())) ->settable($this->table) ->newquerywithoutrelationships(); $column($pivotquery); $this->query->getquery()->addnestedwherequery($pivotquery->getquery(), $boolean); return $this; // returns here, never touches $this->pivotwheres } $this->pivotwheres[] = func get args(); // string form gets recorded here return $this->where($this->qualifypivotcolumn($column), $operator, $value, $boolean); } detach(), updateexistingpivot(), and newpivotstatementforid() all go through interactswithpivottable::newpivotquery(), which builds its query only from $this->pivotwheres (plus pivotwhereins/pivotwherenulls) (interactswithpivottable.php { $query = $this->newpivotstatement(); foreach ($this->pivotwheres as $arguments) { $query->where(...$arguments); } // .... return $query->where($this->getqualifiedforeignpivotkeyname(), $this->parent->{$this->parentkey}); } since the closure branch never get appended to pivotwheres, that condition simply doesn't exist as far as newpivotquery() is concerned.. so, detach() operates on the entire unscoped pivot table for that parent, silently deleting rows it shouldn't touch. though the string form of wherepivot() does not have this problem, since it already correctly records into pivotwheres. this is a data-loss risk: the closure scope reads as if it restricts the relation everywhere (as the string form does, as it was supposed to), but detach()/updateexistingpivot() quietly bypass it. and this isn't limited to only detach()/updateexistingpivot(). orwherepivot() (belongstomany.php, so it hits the same closure branch and hit the same gap. sync() (interactswithpivottable.php → getcurrentlyattachedpivotsforids() (interactswithpivottable.php - same unscoped builder detach() uses. so the closure scope is dropped before sync() even diffs against the given ids: so a $user->activeroles()->sync([...]) can detach rows that were never in the scope, since the "current" set it diffs against silently includes out-of-scope rows. steps to reproduce given a user belongstomany role setup with a pivot table role user that has an active boolean column: php // suppose role user pivot rows for user 1: role 1 (active=1), role 2 (active=1), role 3 (active=0) class user extends model { public function activeroles() { return $this->belongstomany(role::class) ->wherepivot(fn ($query) => $query->where('active', 1)); } } php $user = user::find(1); $user->activeroles()->detach(); // expected: only pivot rows where active = 1 are removed (roles 1 and 2), role 3 stays // actual currently: all pivot rows for user 1 get removed, including role 3 for comparison, the equivalent string-form scope behaves correctly and only detaches the intended rows: php $user->belongstomany(role::class)->wherepivot('active', 1)->detach(); // correctly leaves role 3 (active = 0) untouched

selfbuilding factory is bypassed after a previous resolution throws an exception laravel version 13.x-dev (cdbd17f7e3257e8ae4207d3c3bef6058452d5f72) php version 8.5.10 database driver & version n/a description when a selfbuilding::newinstance() factory throws an exception, the container retains the class in its buildstack. a subsequent resolution of the same class through the same container skips the factory and constructs the object directly. this can bypass validation or initialization performed by the factory. the existing aolinstantmessengerconfig integration-test fixture demonstrates the problem: its factory rejects an away-message duration below 60, but after the first validationexception, a second resolution returns an object with duration 5. expected behavior: each independent resolution should invoke the factory and reject the invalid configuration. the factory's intentional recursive app()->build(static::class) call should continue to work while the factory is active. the stack entry is added by container::buildselfbuildinginstance(), but its array pop() only runs when the factory returns normally. the nested container::call() does not own this entry because the class is already on the stack. steps to reproduce 1. use the framework checkout at the commit above with its development dependencies installed. 2. open tests/integration/container/buildableintegrationtest.php, preserve the initial valid configuration and assertions. replace the final single try/catch with the following loop, keeping the existing config(['aim.away message.duration' => 5]); immediately before it: php for ($attempt = 1; $attempt app->make(aolinstantmessengerconfig::class); $this->fail("expected a validation exception on attempt {$attempt}."); } catch (validationexception $exception) { $this->assertarrayhaskey('away message.duration', $exception->errors()); $this->assertstringcontainsstring('60', $exception->errors()['away message.duration'][0]); } } 4. run: bash vendor/bin/phpunit tests/integration/container/buildableintegrationtest.php --filter test build method can resolve itself via container the two attempts use the same application/container, without flushing or recreating it. actual result: the first attempt throws the expected validationexception; the second returns normally and the test fails with: text expected a validation exception on attempt 2. expected result: both attempts throw validationexception. i reproduced this failure before changing production code. locally, putting the factory call inside try and moving its stack cleanup into finally makes the regression pass. the expanded test also verifies recovery on the same container after setting duration to 60 and body to back online, using the fixture's existing recursive build path.

facades and the container instance point to different applications after route:cache laravel version 13.30.0 and 13.30.1 (13.29.0 is fine) php version 8.5.10 (also 8.5.9) database driver & version not involved. reproduced on the default sqlite of a fresh install and on postgresql 17. description since 61346 (13.30.0) routecachecommand::getfreshapplication() boots a throwaway application and afterwards restores the facade root to the live application: php facade::clearresolvedinstances(); facade::setfacadeapplication($this->laravel); new application also calls container::setinstance($this) (in registerbasebindings()), and nothing restores that. so after route:cache the process is in a split state: facades resolve against the live app, while container::getinstance() / app() resolve against the discarded one. before 13.30 both pointed at the throwaway app, which was equally wrong but self-consistent, so it never showed. optimize runs view:cache right after route:cache in the same process, and view:cache falls into the split: 1. viewclearcommand / viewcachecommand resolve the blade engine through $this->laravel['view.engine.resolver']->resolve('blade'), i.e. on the live app. 2. the blade engine closure in viewserviceprovider::registerbladeengine() builds the engine from container::getinstance()->make('blade.compiler'), i.e. the throwaway app's compiler. 3. that resolution fires the afterresolving('blade.compiler') hooks. a package that registers class component namespaces there through the blade facade (inertia-laravel 3.x does: blade::componentnamespace('inertia\\view\\components', 'inertia')) registers them on the live app's compiler instead. 4. the compiler that actually compiles has an empty classcomponentnamespaces, and the first tag fails: views .......................................................... 9.32ms fail in componenttagcompiler.php line 315: unable to locate a class or view for component [inertia::head]. php artisan view:cache on its own succeeds (no route:cache ran before it in that process). 13.29.0 succeeds. 13.30.x with getfreshapplication() reverted to the 13.29 body succeeds. instrumented run on 13.30.0 (ids from spl object id; 4 is the live app, 2531 the throwaway app booted by route:cache): inertia callback: providerapp 2531 passedcompiler 4100 facadeapp 4 facadecompiler 4463 componentclass(inertia::app): compiler 4100 namespaces=[] facadeapp 4 container 2531 the namespace went to compiler 4463, the compilation ran on 4100. inertia could dodge this particular symptom by using the compiler instance passed to its callback instead of the facade (reported separately to inertiajs/inertia-laravel), but the split between facade::getfacadeapplication() and container::getinstance() is in the framework and affects anything that runs after route:cache in the same process and goes through app() / container::getinstance(). steps to reproduce sh composer create-project laravel/laravel repro 13.30.1 cd repro composer require inertiajs/inertia-laravel 3.3.1 cat > resources/views/app.blade.php blade php artisan optimize views fail: unable to locate a class or view for component [inertia::head] php artisan optimize:clear php artisan view:cache ok composer require laravel/framework:13.29.0 -w php artisan optimize config / events / routes / views all done suggested fix restore the container instance together with the facade root: php protected function getfreshapplication() { return tap(require $this->laravel->bootstrappath('app.php'), function ($app) { $app->make(consolekernelcontract::class)->bootstrap(); facade::clearresolvedinstances(); facade::setfacadeapplication($this->laravel); container::setinstance($this->laravel); }); } configcachecommand::getfreshconfiguration() boots a throwaway app the same way and leaves container::getinstance() on it too; 61350 / 61351 proposed the facade-only restore for it, so whatever lands there should keep the two in sync as well. workarounds until then: run config:cache, event:cache, route:cache, view:cache as separate processes instead of optimize, or pin laravel/framework:13.29.0.

typeerror in sessionguard::userfromrecaller() when remember-me cookie is stale (v12.69.0) laravel version 12.69.0 php version 8.3.30 database driver & version mysql 8 description after upgrading to laravel v12.69.0, any request that calls auth::check() / auth::user() while a stale remember-me cookie is present throws: typeerror: hash equals(): argument 1 ($known string) must be of type string, null given this started with 61386 (ensure password hash matches stored cookie before authenticating the user). when retrievebytoken() returns null (token rotated, user deleted, mismatched cookie, etc.), the new code still calls hash equals(): php $this->viaremember = ! is null($user = $this->provider->retrievebytoken( $recaller->id(), $recaller->token() )); $userpassword = $this->viaremember ? $user->getauthpassword() : null; $recallerhash = $recaller->hash(); return (hash equals($this->hashpasswordforcookie($userpassword), $recallerhash) || hash equals($userpassword, $recallerhash)) ? $user : null; steps to reproduce 1. install laravel 12.69.0 with session auth (auth::attempt($credentials, remember: true) or auth::login($user, true)). 2. log in so the remember web cookie is set. 3. in the database, change that user's remember token to a different value (do not log out in the browser). 4. delete only the session cookie (laravel session). leave remember web . 5. visit any route that calls auth::check() (including /). result: typeerror from illuminate\auth\sessionguard::userfromrecaller(). on 12.68.0 the same steps only result in a guest user.

size rules leak brick\math numberformatexception because their catch targets illuminate's mathexception, not brick's laravel version: v13.24.0 php version: 8.5.10 brick/math version: 0.18.0 database driver & version: n/a description every size-rule comparison in illuminate\validation\concerns\validatesattributes wraps its bignumber::of(...) call in a try { ... } catch (mathexception) block (validatemax, validatemin, validatesize, validatebetween, validategt/gte/lt/lte, validatedecimal, and the date/digit helpers; about 14 sites). the file imports two different exception types: php use brick\math\exception\mathexception as brickmathexception; // line 7 use illuminate\support\exceptions\mathexception; // line 22 so the unaliased catch (mathexception) blocks catch only illuminate's class. that class is thrown by ensureexponentwithinallowedrange() (the scientific-notation guard) and by the multiple of wrapper, which converts brick's exception explicitly: php } catch (brickmathexception $e) { throw new mathexception('an error occurred while handling the multiple of input values.', previous: $e); } no such conversion exists on the size-rule paths. bignumber::of() throws brick's numberformatexception, which implements brick's mathexception interface but is unrelated to illuminate's class, so it escapes every one of those catch blocks and surfaces as an unhandled exception (a 500) instead of a failed validation. two ways to hit it: 1. data-driven: an inf or nan float under a numeric rule. is numeric(inf) is true, so getsize() takes the numeric path and stringifies it to 'inf', which bignumber::of() rejects. on php 8.5, nan additionally emits the new "unexpected nan value was coerced to string" warning from trim() first. 2. developer error that used to fail soft: a non-numeric bound such as max:abc on a numeric attribute reaches bignumber::of('abc') through the same block. steps to reproduce php use illuminate\support\facades\validator; validator::make(['value' => inf], ['value' => ['numeric', 'max:5.5']])->passes(); // brick\math\exception\numberformatexception: value "inf" does not represent a valid number. validator::make(['value' => 5], ['value' => ['numeric', 'max:abc']])->passes(); // brick\math\exception\numberformatexception: value "abc" does not represent a valid number. expected: the rule fails (returns false) the way every other malformed comparison inside these try blocks does, or a framework-typed exception is raised deliberately. suggested fix either add brickmathexception to the size-rule catches (catch (mathexception|brickmathexception)), or convert brick parse failures into illuminate\support\exceptions\mathexception at the boundary (getsize() / trim()), mirroring what validatemultipleof already does. the first is a two-token change per site and preserves the existing "malformed comparison fails validation" semantics.

request::all() discards an uploaded file when a non-file part shares its field name (13.25 behaviour change) laravel version 13.27.0 (behaviour introduced in 13.25.0) php version 8.5.8 database driver & version n/a description since 61099 (13.25.0), request::all() prefers text input over uploaded files on a colliding key, and 61221 refined that while deliberately keeping the precedence. this is not a request to revert it. it is a report that the change silently breaks a widely deployed upload pattern, plus a question about whether that warrants an upgrade-guide note. the conflict filepond) { formdata.append(name, json.stringify(metadata)); } ... formdata.append(name, item.file, / ... /); item metadata defaults to {} and isobject({}) is true, so this part is sent on every upload, not only when metadata is set. i verified the line is present in every published filepond release from 1.0.2 (2018) through 4.32.10 — it has never changed. the request therefore contains two parts named file: content-disposition: form-data; name="file" {} --boundary content-disposition: form-data; name="file"; filename="resume.pdf" content-type: application/pdf php parses this correctly — $ post['file'] === '{}' and $ files['file'] holds the real upload. both superglobals are populated. only the all() merge collapses them. | version | request::all() | wins | |---|---|---| | ≤ 13.24.0 | array replace recursive($this->input(), $this->allfiles()) | files | | 13.25.0 ( 61099) | array replace recursive($this->allfiles(), $this->input()) | input | | ≥ 13.26.0 ( 61221) | array replace recursive($input, $this->allfiles(), $input) | input | through 13.24 the metadata string lost the collision and was harmlessly overwritten by the file, so this never surfaced. from 13.25 it wins, and $request->all()['file'] is the string "{}". impact any endpoint validating $request->all() now rejects every upload, of every file type: php validator::make($request->all(), ['file' => ['required', 'file']]); // "the file field must be a file." this is easy to misdiagnose. both libraries behave exactly as documented, nothing errors, and the failure surfaces as a file-validation message — so it reads as a corrupt-file or unsupported-type problem. it also appears only after an unrelated dependency refresh, with no release-note entry pointing at the cause. workaround for anyone hitting this in the meantime: re-applying the files over all() restores the pre-13.25 precedence generically, without having to name each file field. php $input = array replace recursive($request->all(), $request->allfiles()); files are the override here rather than the base, so this does not reintroduce the key-ordering problem 61221 fixed. as a macro, registered in a service provider: php request::macro('allpreferringfiles', function (): array { return array replace recursive($this->all(), $this->allfiles()); }); // validator::make($request->allpreferringfiles(), $rules); verified on 13.27.0 across four shapes: | case | all() | with re-merge | |---|---|---| | ['file' => '{}'] colliding with uploaded file | string | uploadedfile | | nested profile.avatar collision, non-colliding sibling file | string | uploadedfile (sibling untouched) | | items key order, per 61221's repro | [0, 1] | [0, 1] | | no collision at all | uploadedfile | uploadedfile (no-op) | if you'd rather not touch the whole request, the per-field form works too, since the file bag is unaffected: $request->file('file'). question is $request->file() the intended accessor when a name collides? the test added in 61099 asserts it still returns the uploadedfile, which suggests yes. if so, an upgrade-guide entry would save people meaningful debugging time — and if not, a carve-out that lets a genuine uploadedfile win over a scalar of the same name would resolve it without giving up the intent of 61099. steps to reproduce framework only, no dependencies: php $file = new illuminate\http\uploadedfile( file , 'resume.pdf', null, null, true); $request = illuminate\http\request::create('/', 'post', ['file' => '{}'], [], ['file' => $file]); get debug type($request->all()['file']); // 13.25.0+: string (≤13.24.0: uploadedfile) get debug type($request->file('file')); // uploadedfile (unchanged) over http, against a route running validator::make($request->all(), ['file' => ['required', 'file']]): bash curl -f 'file={}' -f 'file=@resume.pdf' ≤13.24.0: passes 13.25.0+: "the file field must be a file." curl -f 'meta={}' -f 'file=@resume.pdf' passes on all versions — only the shared name triggers it verified on 13.27.0 / php 8.5.8; the ≤13.24.0 behaviour follows from the merge order in the table above.

request()->clamp('my-var') results in 500 if my-var is empty or string laravel version 13.24 php version 8.4.x database driver & version n/a description currently the clamp function for request returns a 500 error if a non-string or empty value is present in the param (ex: our instinct is that a fallback to the default value or the min value would be a more appropriate result than a 500 exception. the signature for the method in laravel's request class is: php public function clamp($key, $min, $max, $default = 0) { return number::clamp($this->data($key, $default), $min, $max); } and the resulting errors happens in arg 1 of number::clamp() because $this->data() results in potentially a string or null value here. because this error happens inside the framework i'd like to open a pr that handles this by using the $this->integer() call instead. php public function clamp($key, $min, $max, $default = 0) { // return number::clamp($this->data($key, $default), $min, $max); return number::clamp($this->integer($key, $default), $min, $max); } but i could also see this just falling back to $default as well...any guidance before i get started would be appreciated. steps to reproduce have a $request->clamp() for a param that is empty. see example above.

renamed config file causes wrong image driver to load laravel version 13.29.0 php version 8.5.9 database driver & version no response description i was an early adopter of the new native laravel image manipulation method after the old package for image intervention was starting to act up. so i installed it on version 13.20 and published the config file, so i could change the default image driver to imagick, as that's what i'm using in all my environments. so changing it in the config file made more sense to me than editing multiple .env files. however with bigger files i started having trouble and got memory errors that i didn't get before. only today i discoverd that the config file image.php was renamed to images.php and therefore my existing config file was ignored and it used the package default which was set to gd. and gd has those memory problems. so the fix was simple: rename the config file in my application as well. but i was kinda baffled that this breaking change wasn't documented clearly anywhere. so if such a breaking change is introduced in a minor version, i would suggest that some sort of fallback and/or error message about using an older config file would be used somewhere, at least until the next major version of laravel where usually these sorts of things are documented very well in the upgrade guide. also i would suggest that a warning is added in the documentation to make it clear to other early adopters this breaking change has happened. steps to reproduce - install laravel 13.20.0 - php artisan config:publish image - change the default image driver in image.php to imagick - confirm that imagick is being used with dd(image::getdefaultdriver());. - composer update - confirm that gd is being used now with dd(image::getdefaultdriver()); and to fix: simply rename config/image.php to config/images.php confirm that imagick is being used again with dd(image::getdefaultdriver());.

redis tagged cache: entries written concurrently with flush() are never invalidated again laravel version 13.4.0 php version 8.5.5 (phpredis 6.3.0) database driver & version redis 7.4.8 (cache store), mysql 8.0 description redistaggedcache::forever() registers the entry in the tag set before it writes the value: php public function forever($key, $value) { $key = enum value($key); $this->tags->addentry($this->itemkey($key)); return parent::forever($key, $value); } flush() deletes exactly what the tag set lists — its lua script does del on the key and zrem on the member. if a flush() from another request lands between those two statements: 1. it reads our member from the tag set, 2. del is a no-op, because the value key does not exist yet, 3. zrem removes the reference, 4. our set then writes the value. the result is a key that exists in redis but is referenced by no tag set. since flush() can only delete what the tag set lists, no subsequent invalidation can ever reach that key . written through forever() / rememberforever() it also carries no ttl, so it keeps serving its stale value indefinitely. put(), add(), increment() and decrement() register the tag entry before the write in the same way. this is the mirror image of the problem that was fixed on the flush side: flush() no longer deletes the tag set key, and its del plus zrem are atomic. the write path still performs its two operations in the order that makes a concurrent flush harmful. expected behaviour every key that exists in the keyspace should be reachable by an invalidation, so the number of entries not referenced by any tag set should be 0. impact this is not only a keyspace leak — the orphaned entry keeps being served. in our case (an appointment booking system) the cached availability query for one department and one day became permanently stale, and a fully booked time slot kept being offered as free. exactly one entry out of 800 was affected, which made it look random and unreproducible. it only became visible by scanning the keyspace and comparing every key against the tag-set members. a restart or a full cache:clear makes the symptom disappear, and it then takes weeks to build up again — which is why this is easy to misdiagnose as fixed by an unrelated change. the stored values themselves are never wrong. in the runs below each entry stored its own key name as its value; all 1,767,563 reads returned either the correct value or a miss, and every remaining key still held the value it was written with. the entries are not corrupted, they are unreachable — which is why this surfaces as "stale forever" rather than as garbage data. proposed fix write the value first, register it afterwards: diff public function forever($key, $value) { $key = enum value($key); - $this->tags->addentry($this->itemkey($key)); + $result = parent::forever($key, $value); - return parent::forever($key, $value); + if ($result) { + $this->tags->addentry($this->itemkey($key)); + } + + return $result; } diff public function put($key, $value, $ttl = null) { $key = enum value($key); if (is null($ttl)) { return $this->forever($key, $value); } $seconds = $this->getseconds($ttl); - if ($seconds > 0) { - $this->tags->addentry( - $this->itemkey($key), - $seconds - ); - } + $result = parent::put($key, $value, $ttl); - return parent::put($key, $value, $ttl); + if ($result && $seconds > 0) { + $this->tags->addentry($this->itemkey($key), $seconds); + } + + return $result; } add(), increment() and decrement() need the same treatment. a flush() running before the registration cannot delete a key it does not know about, and by the time the key is visible to a flush it is registered. every interleaving then ends in either no key or key plus tag member — the state key without tag member becomes unreachable. what remains is an ordinary cache-aside race, where the stored value may be one generation old. that value is invalidatable, so the next flush() clears it. as a side effect the tag entry is now only registered after a write that actually succeeded. residual: a process crash between the two statements still leaves an orphan. closing that too would require set and zadd in a single lua script, mirroring what flush() already does for its own two operations. the reordering alone turns a frequent concurrency hazard into a rare crash hazard. history this opens a new issue as suggested in 47903, which reported the same symptom and was closed with "if this issue can be definitively identified as a bug, feel free to open up a new issue with a link to the original one" . that report showed the signature precisely: flush() returns true and the key survives, while forget() on the same key works — an entry that no tag set references. the flush side of this problem was analysed in 48078: back then flush() deleted the tag set key itself, so entries written concurrently were orphaned. today's implementation no longer does that. what has never been looked at is the write side, which is what this report is about — and that is why reports of the same symptom kept coming in after the flush side was addressed. other reports of the same symptom: - 58047 — a single key under a tag stops invalidating while all others under the same tag work; closed without a root cause, the reporter worked around it by renaming the tag. - discussion 46175 — tag sets growing indefinitely. - discussion 49159 — general concerns about the redis tagged cache implementation. the workarounds people converged on in those threads — capping every tagged entry at a one-hour ttl, or switching to an alternative cache package — are consistent with this cause: a ttl does not prevent the orphan, it just lets it expire on its own. steps to reproduce drop this command into a stock laravel app with cache store=redis. it works with both phpredis and predis: php getstore(); $connection = $store->connection(); $prefix = $store->getprefix(); $deadline = microtime(true) + (float) $this->option('seconds'); if ($this->argument('mode') === 'write') { $count = 0; while (microtime(true) rememberforever('key-'.$count++, fn () => 'payload'); } $this->info("wrote {$count} entries"); return 0; } if ($this->argument('mode') === 'flush') { $count = 0; while (microtime(true) flush(); $count++; } $this->info("flushed {$count} times"); return 0; } $indexed = []; foreach ((array) $connection->zrange($prefix.'tag:race:entries', 0, -1) as $member) { $indexed[$member] = true; } $globalprefix = $connection instanceof phpredisconnection ? (string) $connection->client()->getoption(\redis::opt prefix) : (string) $connection->client()->getoptions()->prefix; $full = $globalprefix.$prefix; $namespace = sha1('tag:race:entries'); $present = []; $cursor = null; do { $result = $connection->scan($cursor, ['match' => $full.$namespace.' ', 'count' => 1000]); if (! is array($result)) { break; } [$cursor, $keys] = $result; foreach ((array) $keys as $key) { $present[substr($key, strlen($full))] = true; } } while ((int) $cursor !== 0); $orphans = array diff key($present, $indexed); $this->line('keys present in redis : '.count($present)); $this->line('members in tag set : '.count($indexed)); $this->line('orphaned entries : '.count($orphans)); cache::tags(['race'])->flush(); $survivors = 0; foreach (array keys($orphans) as $item) { if ($connection->exists($prefix.$item)) { $survivors++; } } $this->line('surviving a fresh flush(): '.$survivors.' of '.count($orphans)); foreach (array keys($present) as $item) { $connection->del($prefix.$item); } $connection->del($prefix.'tag:race:entries'); return 0; } } then run a writer and a flusher concurrently, and check afterwards: bash php artisan tag-race write & php artisan tag-race flush & wait php artisan tag-race check actual result eight seconds of a single writer against a single flusher: flushed 37797 times wrote 24097 entries keys present in redis : 74 members in tag set : 1 orphaned entries : 73 surviving a fresh flush(): 73 of 73 scaling the same setup up to 8 writers, 4 flushers and 4 readers — 1,408,113 writes, 921,090 flushes and 1,767,563 reads, 4,096,766 operations in total: keys present in redis : 201464 members in tag set : 476 orphaned entries : 200988 surviving final flush(): 200988 every one of those 200,988 entries has no ttl and is unreachable by any future flush() of that tag. same reproduction with the proposed fix applied 3,756,447 writes, 2,408,532 flushes and 4,670,690 reads — 10,835,669 operations , same harness: keys present in redis : 0 members in tag set : 0 orphaned entries : 0 value mismatches : 0 surviving final flush(): 0 keys present: 0 is the meaningful part here: an orphan survives every flush by definition, as the 200,988 above demonstrate. had a single one been created during those 10.8 million operations, it would still be sitting in the keyspace. we have been running the reordered store in production through a custom cache driver.

numeric rules throw uncaught brick numberformatexception for is numeric-accepted strings trim() does not clean (e.g. "\x0c5") laravel version 13.24.0 (code verified unchanged at v13.26.1 and current 13.x head) php version 8.5.9 database driver & version n/a (no database involved) description every numeric comparison rule (min, max, size, between, gt, gte, lt, lte) can throw an uncaught brick\math\exception
umberformatexception instead of failing validation, when the value is a string that is numeric() accepts but php's trim() does not clean — for example a form feed (\x0c) adjacent to a digit. in an http context this surfaces as a 500 for input that should simply produce a validation message. the mechanism, with line references to src/illuminate/validation/concerns/validatesattributes.php at v13.26.1: - is numeric("\x0c5") is true (php counts \x0c as leading whitespace for is numeric), so getsize() takes its numeric branch. - getsize() takes its numeric branch and returns the value through $this->trim($value). - $this->trim($value) uses php trim(), whose default charlist (" 	
\0\x0b") does not include \x0c, so the form feed survives. - bignumber::of("\x0c5") (e.g. validatemax(), line 1711) throws brick\math\exception
umberformatexception: value "5" does not represent a valid number. - the surrounding catch (mathexception) (line 1712) refers to illuminate\support\exceptions\mathexception (imported at line 22). brick's exceptions implement brick\math\exception\mathexception — a different, unrelated type (imported at line 7 as brickmathexception) — so nothing catches the throw. the only rule that catches the brick type is validatemultipleof() (line 1976). notes: - over http with the default global middleware, trimstrings (via str::trim, whose \s-based regex does strip \x0c) removes leading/trailing form feeds, which masks the simplest case. the crash remains reachable wherever the validator runs on input that middleware did not clean: direct validator::make() usage, queued/imported data, custom pipelines, or apps that exclude/replace trimstrings. - \x0c is the clearest trigger because it is the one byte is numeric() accepts as padding that trim() does not strip. the class of bug is the type mismatch in the catch, so any future bignumber::of failure mode lands the same way — 55944, 46225, 59555, 59559 and 60697 were earlier reports/proposals in this same class. the natural fix is to widen the catches to catch (mathexception|brickmathexception) — the shape validatemultipleof() already uses in this same trait (and which 59559 proposed for a related trigger). unlike the earlier inf/nan reports, the trigger here is an ordinary request string, not a special float value. found while hardening input handling in an application; happy to pr either direction if the maintainers indicate a preference. steps to reproduce standalone, no app required: php make(['n' => "\x0c5"], ['n' => 'numeric|max:10'])->fails(); "5\x0c" (trailing form feed) throws identically. "\x0c" alone fails cleanly (correct), because is numeric rejects it.

firefox: web platformview content never composites to screen (nested shadow dom + ), despite healthy dom summary on flutter web (canvaskit renderer), a platform view whose native content lives inside a library's own shadow dom — projected into flutter's platform-view via the standard mechanism — renders a fully correct, non-zero-sized, visible dom/css tree in firefox , but the content is never actually painted to the screen. the screen shows only the app's background color. chrome and edge never reproduce this, every time, with the identical build. a manual browser-level layout change (resizing the window) reliably reveals the correctly-rendered content afterward, which is the strongest clue that this is a compositing-step bug, not a dom/css/application-logic bug. this matches the bug category described in 105485 and 193223, but neither of those threads has a confirmed fix or workaround that applies here (both are canvaskit; --wasm/skwasm was checked and documented as reproducing the same category in 193223, and --web-renderer no longer exists as a build flag to test the old html renderer as an a/b). environment - flutter 3.41.1 • channel stable - framework revision 582a0e7c55 - engine revision 3452d735bd (hash cc8e596aa65130a0678cc59613ed1c5125184db4) - dart 3.11.0 - renderer: canvaskit (default;
