listing what was eliminated so this isn't re-litigated by anyone attempting to help: - not a webgl/hardware/driver problem. the official maplibre gl js demo page (a plain top-level page, no flutter, no shadow dom/slot projection) renders correctly in the exact same firefox installation, at the same time. - not application/business logic. added targeted diagnostic logging around every step of the app's own async startup sequence (an initial "welcome banner" animation, a camera-descent animation, lifecycle-state checks). every single step was confirmed completing correctly, in the correct order, with the correct final values (e.g. the map camera's internal state correctly reporting it had moved to the intended location) — and the screen was still blank. this conclusively shows the app's own code is not the cause. - not app-lifecycle-pause related. checked applifecyclestate transitions directly via logging; initial state was correctly resumed; no suspicious transition correlated with the bug. - not a css visibility/sizing bug. direct devtools dom inspection (walking the live tree while the screen was blank) found the entire chain — → → shadow root → → (flutter's own canvas layers) and , as a light-dom sibling inside , → → → — every element correctly created, non-zero-sized, with no display:none/visibility:hidden/ opacity:0 anywhere in the chain. - not a one-time loading-overlay bug in our own app shell. our index.html has a pre-flutter loading spinner overlay removed by a flutter-first-frame event listener. verified directly via dom search while the screen was blank that this overlay element had already been correctly removed from the dom — the underlying (correctly rendered, per the point above) content was simply never composited to the visible screen afterward. - gpu-compositing-layer-promotion css hint had no effect. added transform: translatez(0); will-change: transform; to the platform-view host element, hypothesizing firefox wasn't promoting the nested canvas to its own compositing layer. no change in behavior. - a forced-reflow "resize nudge" (replicating in code what manually resizing the window does) revealed a related, separate finding worth flagging: triggering a real layout mutation (temporarily changing body padding, with a synchronous offsetheight read to force immediate recompute, then reverting) at a sufficiently early point in the app's startup sequence caused flutter's own widget tree to report mounted == false moments later, consistent with flutter tearing down and recreating state in response to that layout change. this suggests that what a user's manual window-resize is actually doing, when it "fixes" the display, might be forcing flutter to dispose and recreate the platform-view's owning widget — succeeding on the second construction where the first (immediately after page load) did not — rather than directly fixing gpu compositing on the existing instance. this was not conclusively confirmed (a deliberate key-based widget rebuild experiment, to test this theory directly rather than via an accidental layout-change side effect, was the next planned step but not completed/reported on as of this issue being filed). related issues - 105485 — platform view isvisible compositing flag determined incorrectly and never re-evaluated; matches our dom-healthy-but-never-painted symptom closely. - 193223 — documents the same async-appended-platform-view-content category reproducing under skwasm too, which is why switching renderers was not pursued as a workaround here. neither thread's suggested workarounds (renderer switch, forcing isvisible via an unrelated pointerinterceptor-specific api) were applicable or available in our version/situation; see "what was ruled out" above. why we think this belongs in the engine/compositor, not the plugin the platform-view's own content (maplibre gl js) is independently verified correct — same js library renders fine on a plain page in the same browser. the dom structure flutter builds around it is independently verified correct (complete, visible, non-zero-sized, no hiding styles anywhere in the chain). the only remaining layer is whatever actually composites/paints the already-correct dom to the visible screen — and a real layout event (resize) reliably fixes it after the fact, which points at a one-time compositing decision made incorrectly at initial paint and never re-evaluated, specifically for firefox, specifically for a platform view whose content lives behind a shadow dom + projection (not a plain top-level platform view). what would help from here - confirmation of whether this is a known, broader instance of 105485/ 193223 specifically for the shadow-dom-wrapped platform-view case, or a distinct bug. - any officially-supported way to force a platform view's compositing state/isvisible flag to be re-evaluated after first paint, usable from application code without needing an unrelated-context api. - confirmation (or denial) of the widget-rebuild-via-key theory above — i.e. whether flutter web platform views are known to render correctly only from their second construction onward under some condition, which would make a deliberate rebuild-after-mount a legitimate application-level workaround rather than a hack.

combined_text: spurious assertion "traversalparentidentifier must be unique" when a keyed row with a tooltip moves to a lower index in a listview steps to reproduce 1. run the main.dart below (it calls semanticsbinding.instance.ensuresemantics(), as an active screen reader would), or run the flutter test snippet. 2. reorder the list (press "reverse" / second pumpwidget). each listview item is an un-keyed column (header + row). the row inside carries a globalkey and contains a tooltip; it moves from item index 2 to item index 1. expected results the list reorders without an exception. actual results the assertion in semanticsowner.sendsemanticsupdate fires (debug/test only, it is an assert): 'package:flutter/src/semantics/semantics.dart': failed assertion: line 5016 pos 13: '! traversalparentnodes.containskey(node. traversalparentidentifier) || traversalparentnodes[node.traversalparentidentifier!] == node': the traversalparentidentifier must be unique. no two semantics nodes can share the same traversalparentidentifier. analysis - every listview item is wrapped in indexedsemantics; its semantics node is bound to the index and absorbs everything mergeable inside the item, including the overlayportal's semantics(traversalparentidentifier: this) of the tooltip (semanticsconfiguration.absorb). - the keyed row moves between items on reorder, so the identifier moves from one live node (old index) to another live node (new index). - sendsemanticsupdate sorts the dirty nodes by depth only, and while visiting a node it only removes the traversalparentnodes entries that point to that node itself . if the new holder is visited before the old holder, the entry still maps to the old node and the assertion fires, although the state after the flush would be consistent. - it is order dependent: moving the tooltip row from index 2 to 1 fails, from index 1 to 2 passes. - it does not happen when the row is the item itself (no un-keyed wrapper), with addsemanticindexes: false, or when the tooltip is wrapped in semantics(container: true) (this is our workaround). - possible fix (untested): in the dirty-node loop, first remove the stale traversalparentnodes entries of all dirty nodes, then register the identifiers in a second pass. tested only on 3.47.0 stable; i have not tried beta/master. related: 191173 describes the same assertion on 3.47.0 and was closed by the stale bot for lack of a reproduction (this issue is that reproduction). 190344 is a different case (two tooltips merged into one item node, absorb keeps only the first identifier). code sample main.dart dart import 'package:flutter/material.dart'; import 'package:flutter/semantics.dart'; void main() { // semantics must be enabled (as with voiceover/talkback/narrator). semanticsbinding.instance.ensuresemantics(); runapp(const myapp()); } class myapp extends statefulwidget { const myapp({super.key}); @override state createstate() => myappstate(); } class myappstate extends state { list order = ['a', 'b', 'p', 'd']; final keys = {}; @override widget build(buildcontext context) { return materialapp( home: scaffold( appbar: appbar( actions: [ textbutton( onpressed: () => setstate(() => order = order.reversed.tolist()), child: const text('reverse'), ), ], ), body: listview.builder( itemcount: order.length, itembuilder: (context, i) { final id = order[i]; [web] fix --web-content-hash breaking cache when --source-maps is used when building a flutter web app with both --web-content-hash and --source-maps (e.g., flutter build web --wasm --web-content-hash --source-maps or flutter build web --web-content-hash --source-maps), build/web/precache manifest.json records "urlhashed": false and a mismatched "hash" for main.dart. .js: json { "url": "main.dart.216ed961.js", "hash": "fca793b5", "size": 6079674, "urlhashed": false } root cause 1. in hashandrenameweboutput from the initial main.dart.js bytes (when its trailing comment is still // sourcemappingurl=main.dart.js.map), derives newbasename = 'main.dart.216ed961.js', and then rewrites the trailing sourcemappingurl directive inside main.dart.js in-place to // sourcemappingurl=main.dart.216ed961.js.map before renaming the file on disk ( additionally stripping any trailing newline due to \s $ matching \n before eof). 2. later, during webreleasebundle.build, updateprecachemanifest. 3. because 'main.dart.216ed961.js'.contains('.fca793b5.') is false, updateprecachemanifest sets "urlhashed": false and "hash": "fca793b5", breaking cache validation and precache manifest consumers that rely on urlhashed: true and filename/content hash parity. other affected files - main.dart. .js (dart2jstarget and the js fallback in --wasm builds): affected when --source-maps is passed. - main.dart. .mjs.map (dart2wasmtarget): if a .mjs.map file is present alongside main.dart.mjs, dart2wasmtarget previously derived jssupportmapname = '$jssupportname.map'. - flutter service worker.js / worker. .js : uses hashandrenameweboutput with sourcemapfile if present. - main.dart. .wasm : not affected ( hashandrenameweboutput skips sourcemappingurl rewriting when iswasm is true because .wasm embeds main.dart.wasm.map in a binary custom section). proposed fix (hash inversion) in hashandrenameweboutput (packages/flutter tools/lib/src/build system/targets/web.dart): 1. hash sourcemapfile first (maphash) and rename it via computehashedbasename(oldmapbasename, maphash, file.filesystem) (producing main.dart. .js.map, main.dart. .mjs.map, worker. .js.map). 2. rewrite // sourcemappingurl= in file (using positive lookahead (?=\s $) so trailing newlines are preserved). 3. compute contenthash from the final bytes of file and rename file to main.dart. .js so its filename hash matches its on-disk bytes and updateprecachemanifest records "urlhashed": true with the matching "hash". 4. resolve mainjsmapname in dart2jstarget.buildfiles and jssupportmapname in dart2wasmtarget.buildfiles via resolvehashedbasename.

unittests.cc: build the tree 0 > [1 > 3 > 4], 2, 5 > 6, then send one commit with 1 without child 3, 2 claiming 3, and 5 without child 6 (nodes 3 and 4 not sent). then walk every delegate's children. expected results either the update is rejected atomically (the tree and the bridge stay at the previous consistent state) or it is applied consistently (delegates and cached child counts match the tree). later commits keep applying. actual results 1. accessibilitybridge::commitupdates first removes the child from its old parent, then applies a second update that passes axtree::computependingchanges but fails in validatependingchangescomplete ("nodes left pending by the update: 3"), after updatenode has already run deleteoldchildren (nodes freed) and created new nodes. 2. axtree::unserialize returns false before the observer notifications and before the unignored-child cache refresh. the bridge therefore keeps delegates whose ax node is freed, has no delegate for the new nodes, and leaves parents whose cached unignored child count exceeds their real children. 3. commitupdates gates on the sticky axtree::error() string (never cleared) instead of the return value, and its first-update error path is an assert(false) that release builds compile out and that returns without clearing the pending updates. every later commit is refused, so the bridge never recovers. 4. the next appkit query dereferences the stale state. two field signatures from a shipping app, symbolized against the release fluttermacos: - a mouse-moved tracking-area update: -[fluttertextfield frame] (fluttertextinputsemanticsobject.mm:97) into fluttertextplatformnode::getframe (:186) into axtree::relativetotreebounds on a freed axnode. - an out-of-process ax query (nsaccessibilitychildren): -[axplatformnodecocoa axchildreninternal] (ax platform node mac.mm:651) into flutterplatformnodedelegate::childatindex (flutter platform node delegate.cc:90), fault address 0x48 (axnodedata::id read through a null child): getchildcount() returned the stale cached count and getunignoredchildatindex(index) returned nullptr. in the unit cell: the bridge logs failed to update ui::axtree, error: nodes left pending by the update: 3, the delegate for 6 outlives its node, node 3 has no delegate, node 5 reports one unignored child while getunignoredchildatindex(0) is null, and the walk crashes with exc bad access (code=1, address=0x48), frame 0 ui::axnode::id(this=0x0) (ax node.h:110), frame 1 flutterplatformnodedelegate::childatindex(index=0) (flutter platform node delegate.cc:90). a second cell in fluttertextinputsemanticsobjecttest.mm, same commit with 6 a text field: the dropped fluttertextfield stays attached to the view and its frame reads the freed node. a plain move (a node moved and sent) is safe at this pin: the bridge's two updates delete and recreate the node and replace its delegate. what we changed locally (happy to send it as a pr) - accessibility bridge.{h,cc}: commitupdates branches on the unserialize return value, logs the error, and calls a new recoverfromfailedupdate that drops delegates whose node the tree no longer holds, creates delegates for tree nodes that have none, recomputes every node's unignored child cache, and clears the pending updates and queued events. nothing gates on the sticky error string any more, so later commits apply and fire events normally. - flutter platform node delegate.{h,cc}: a delegate whose node lives in its bridge's tree resolves the node by id (a new ownerbridge::getnodefromtree) on every call, and every accessor answers the empty value when the node is gone (0 children, a null child, empty data, an empty rect, no parent, no ancestor, false from accessibilityperformaction). childatindex guards a null getunignoredchildatindex. - fluttertextinputsemanticsobject.mm: fluttertextplatformnode::getframe answers nszerorect when the node is gone. flutterplatformnodedelegatemac.mm and flutter platform node delegate windows.cc guard their one direct getaxnode() use. with the patch the two cells pass, common cpp unittests passes 234 of 234, and the macos accessibility and bundled native assets are not resolved from the bundle on embedder-api platforms: "relative" resolves against a debug label a bundled native asset is recorded by bare file name on a desktop build, and the engine hands that to dlopen, so it resolves through the dynamic linker instead of from the bundle. the manifest has a relative kind that should cover this, but on embedder-api platforms it resolves against a debug label, so it cannot be used either. a packaged app therefore has no way to load its own bundled native assets without putting their directory on the global linker search path. verified at 3.47.5. the tool writes a bare name flutter tools/lib/src/isolated/native assets/native assets.dart, targetlocationsinglearchitecture: dart case dynamicloadingbundled : final string filename = asset.codeasset.file!.pathsegments.last; if (absolutepath != null) { // flutter tester needs full host paths. uri = absolutepath.resolve(filename); } else { // flutter desktop needs "absolute" paths inside the app. uri = uri(path: filename); } absolutepath is non-null only for the tester: final uri? absolutepath = fluttertester ? builduri : null;. so a real build emits a name with no directory: json {"format-version":[1,0,0],"native-assets":{"linux riscv64":{ "package:sqlite3/src/ffi/libsqlite3.g.dart":["system","libsqlite3.so"], "package:appstream dart/src/appstream native.dart":["absolute","libappstream.so"]}}} the engine dlopens it as-is runtime/dart isolate.cc nativeassetsdlopen sends kabsolute to dart::bin::nativeassets::dlopenabsolute, which is dlopen of that string. with no slash the dynamic linker resolves it: dt runpath, ld library path, ld.so.cache, default directories. the asset store is not consulted -- nativeassetsmanager parses the manifest and nothing else (assets/native assets.cc). bundling the library is therefore not enough. its directory has to go on the global search path, which puts every app's libraries in one namespace: two apps bundling different versions of a library get whichever ld.so.cache lists first. relative cannot be used flutter tools documents the kind as what we want: dart // "relative" in the context of native assets would be relative to the // kernel or aot snapshot. the engine resolves it against advisory script uri: cpp static void nativeassetsdlopenrelative(const char path, char error) { const std::string& script uri = ( isolate group data)->getadvisoryscripturi(); return dart::bin::nativeassets::dlopenrelative(path, script uri.data(), error); } that is a debug label, not a path. common/settings.h defaults it to "main.dart", and nothing exposes it to an embedder: - shell/platform/embedder/embedder.cc never sets it, and no flutterprojectargs field maps to it - shell/common/switches.{h,cc} has no switch, so command line argv cannot carry it - only the in-tree ios and fuchsia embedders set it, from libraryuri and debug label dlopenrelative merges paths per rfc 3986 (runtime/bin/uri.cc): cpp const char last slash = strrchr(base path, '/'); if (last slash == nullptr) { // there is no slash in the base path. return the ref path unchanged. return makecopyofstring(ref path); } "main.dart" has no slash, so the reference reaches dlopen unchanged and resolves against the process working directory. under an init system that is arbitrary. nothing available today is both relocatable and isolated | | installed | side-loaded | per-app isolation | |---|---|---|---| | bare name plus a global search path entry | works | needs ld library path | no, one namespace | | rewrite the manifest to an absolute install path | works | breaks, path does not exist | yes | | relative | -- | -- | unusable, above | suggestions 1. resolve bundled assets against the asset store. nativeassetsmanager already holds the assetmanager; resolving against native assets/ / in the bundle makes the bare name the tool already emits work everywhere, with no manifest or embedder change. 2. give relative a base that is a path -- the asset store or the snapshot -- so the kind means what flutter tools says it means. 3. expose advisory script uri through flutterprojectargs or a switch. cheapest, but only helps embedders that adopt the field. happy to do any of these as a pr if you say which you would take. context: packaging flutter for embedded linux with yocto, across flutter-gtk, ivi-homescreen and flutter-pi. all are embedder-api hosts, so none can set advisory script uri. flutter doctor -v [✓] flutter (channel stable, 3.47.5, on fedora linux 44 (workstation edition) 7.2.7-200.fc44.x86 64, locale en us.utf-8) [14ms] • flutter version 3.47.5 on channel stable at /mnt/raid10/yocto/.p0d/flutter • upstream repository • framework revision 6a19cca564 (13 days ago), 2026-09-17 14:13:22 -0400 • engine revision af7e796e16 • dart version 3.13.4 • devtools version 2.60.0 • feature flags: enable-web, enable-linux-desktop, enable-macos-desktop, enable-windows-desktop, enable-android, enable-ios, cli-animations, enable-native-assets, enable-record-use, enable-swift-package-manager, omit-legacy-version-file, enable-lldb-debugging, enable-uiscene-migration [✗] android toolchain - develop for android devices [8ms] ✗ unable to locate android sdk. install android studio from: on first launch it will assist you in installing the android sdk components. combined_text: tooltip (overlayportal) of a list item parked in the keep-alive bucket is never laid out but still hit-tested, freezing mouse input steps to reproduce 1. a lazily built list (listview.builder, default addautomatickeepalives: true) whose items contain a tooltip around an iconbutton, with no relayout boundary between the item root and the tooltip (a loose-height column/row, as in most cards). 2. the mouse enters an item's iconbutton: the inkwell hover highlight makes the item request keep-alive, and the tooltip shows its overlay (a new renderdeferredlayoutbox is added to the root rendertheater). 3. in the same frame, the list scrolls so that this item ends up past the trailing cache extent (for example a fast wheel or trackpad flick upwards). 4. move the mouse. two deterministic repros below: a widget test (fails on 3.47.3 and 3.49.0-0.1.pre), and a small web app plus a devtools console snippet that freezes a release build in chrome. expected results the tooltip overlay is either laid out, or not hit-tested/painted while its anchor is parked. pointer input keeps working. actual results rendersliverlist.performlayout collects the item as trailing garbage without laying it out, and destroyorcachechild parks it in the keep-alive bucket, still attached. the new renderdeferredlayoutbox is only laid out through its layout surrogate (inside the parked item, which is never laid out again) or during the theater's own layout (which adddeferredchild does not dirty), so it never gets a size. rendertheatermixin.hittestchildren still hit-tests it: - debug: cannot hit test a render box that has never been laid out. with semantics enabled, the semantics flush asserts first: '!childsemantics.renderobject. needslayout': is not true. - release (dart2js): null check operator used on a null value in renderbox.hittest. it throws in mousetracker's post-frame device update and on every following pointer event, before the hover exit is dispatched. so the inkwell never loses its highlight, the item stays kept alive, the tooltip stays on screen, and the app stops reacting to the mouse until the page is reloaded . in debug, the tracker then also asserts '! debugduringdeviceupdate': is not true. not affected: items with a relayout boundary inside (for example sizedbox(height: …) + align), because the dirty boundary is still laid out from the dirty list while parked; and leading garbage, because rendersliverlist lays those children out before collecting them. in production we hit this in our production flutter web app (desktop chrome, edge and safari; flutter 3.45 beta, 3.47 and 3.49 beta), in a side-panel list of cards that each have a delete iconbutton with a tooltip. over the last 90 days: - 37 users hit it at least once, about 1.7 % of the 2,125 web users who opened that page; - 14,415 error events, since a frozen tab throws on every mouse move until it is reloaded; - mostly on low-end laptops (for example a 1358×644 screen with 4 gb of ram). the hover and a large scroll delta have to land in the same frame, which slow frames make likely because wheel events get coalesced. we reproduced it in a release web build by dispatching a pointermove onto a tooltip button and a −1200 px wheel event in the same task. workaround we shipped: swallowing keepalivenotification between the tooltip and its inkwell (notificationlistener (onnotification: ( ) => true, child: …)), so a hovered item that scrolls out of range is disposed with its tooltip instead of being parked. possible direction, for you to judge: skip deferred children that were never laid out in rendertheatermixin.hittestchildren (and paint), or make sure a deferred child added while its surrogate cannot be laid out still gets a layout. related: 186564 fixed the detached-surrogate case, but parked keep-alive children stay attached. the relevant code is unchanged on master since 3.49 (reformat only). code sample code sample dart import [image picker android] re-encoding opaque pngs returns jpeg bytes with a .png filename steps to reproduce 1. create a flutter android app with image picker 1.2.3 and image picker android 0.8.13+19. 2. pick an opaque rgb png from the gallery with maxwidth set and imagequality below 100, for example maxwidth: 2048 and imagequality: 85. 3. read the returned xfile name and the first bytes from xfile.readasbytes(). 4. upload the returned bytes using the xfile name to a server that validates file extension against detected image format. expected results the returned file name and bytes should describe the same image format. if the image is encoded as jpeg, its returned name should use a .jpg extension; otherwise the png bytes should be preserved with a .png extension. actual results in image picker android 0.8.13+19, imageresizer.resizeimageifneeded performs a transformation whenever maxwidth/maxheight is non-null or imagequality is below 100. the output is created with the original image name prefixed by scaled , so its extension is retained. createimageonexternaldirectory chooses png only when bitmap.hasalpha() is true; otherwise it compresses the bitmap as jpeg. therefore an opaque png can be returned with a .png name while its bytes are jpeg. a server that derives expected mime from the name and validates the byte signature rejects the upload as an invalid image format. this matches the failure observed in our android release app. the source is available in imageresizer.java in flutter/packages, under packages/image picker/image picker android/android/src/main/java/io/flutter/plugins/imagepicker/. code sample import 'package:image picker/image picker.dart'; future pickandinspect() async { final file = await imagepicker().pickimage( source: imagesource.gallery, maxwidth: 2048, imagequality: 85, ); if (file == null) return; final bytes = await file.readasbytes(); final signature = bytes .take(3) .map((value) => value.toradixstring(16).padleft(2, '0')) .join(); print('name: ' + file.name); print('first three bytes: ' + signature); } for a png decoded without alpha, the reported name remains .png while the jpeg signature is expected to start with ffd8ff. screenshots or video not applicable. logs adb confirmed that the system picker returned an image and android decoded a bitmap. the release app does not log multipart request/response bodies, and the picker uri grant did not allow reading the selected file from the adb shell. the exact bytes and alpha flag of the failing image were therefore not independently captured from that release run; the format mismatch above follows from the pinned dependency source. flutter doctor output the full flutter doctor -v output from the release build environment is unavailable. the repository mobile ci pins flutter stable 3.44.9. the dependency versions are image picker 1.2.3 and image picker android 0.8.13+19. related issues flutter/flutter 121878 reported an earlier android filename/content mismatch in the opposite direction: png bytes were given a .jpg filename. this report concerns jpeg bytes retaining a .png filename after image resizing/quality processing.

after a three-finger screenshot, flutter touch handling stays in accepted and subsequent touches stop responding problem on an android tablet, after using the system three-finger swipe-down screenshot gesture, none of the note cards in our flutter page respond to taps. the list can still scroll vertically. restarting the application that provides the flutter page restores tapping. this happens every time on the current device. logging confirms that after the screenshot, both down and up from subsequent taps reach flutter, but the cards' ontap callbacks no longer run. the three old pointers from the screenshot gesture never end. the list's drag recognizer stays in accepted, and hit-test paths for subsequent taps no longer include the card subtree. here, accepted refers to the state of verticaldraggesturerecognizer in the logs: the drag gesture has been recognized and accepted. background and environment we are developing a launcher (the device's home-screen application) for an android tablet. the launcher is written in kotlin with jetpack compose , with several tabs for different pages. the notes tab displays a flutter page written in dart , provided by a separate android application running in its own process. that application creates a flutterengine and flutterview and uses surfacecontrolviewhost to provide a child surface. the launcher displays this surface through a surfaceview hosted in compose's androidview. the flutter page contains vertically scrollable note cards. the cards are ordinary flutter widgets that handle taps with gesturedetector.ontap. - android 15 / api 35 - flutter 3.44.6 - release mode - flutterview uses the default surface rendering mode - the device supports a built-in three-finger swipe-down screenshot gesture steps to reproduce 1. open the launcher and switch to the flutter notes tab. 2. tap any card and confirm that its ontap callback runs. 3. swipe down with three fingers over the list to trigger a system screenshot. 4. after the screenshot, tap any card again. expected: cards should still respond to taps after the screenshot. actual: none of the cards' ontap callbacks run. the list can still scroll, and other launcher tabs and native components respond normally. restarting the application that provides the flutter page restores tapping. what happens to the next tap the screenshot gesture never ends on the flutter side android logs show that two action pointer up events and the final action up reach the viewrootimpl enqueue point in the process providing the flutter page. however, these events never enter flutterview's dispatchtouchevent / ontouchevent. flutter receives neither the corresponding up events nor a cancel event. so far, we have narrowed the gap down to the path between viewrootimpl enqueueing the events and flutterview's dispatch entry. we have not identified the specific android function that stops these events from reaching flutterview. subsequent taps have complete events but do not hit the cards for taps after the screenshot, the logs show: - both down and up reach flutterview, pointerdatapacket, and dart gesturebinding. - the same verticaldraggesturerecognizer remains in accepted, tracking the three old pointers from the screenshot gesture. - a new pointer is immediately accepted by that drag recognizer. its up removes only that new pointer; the three old pointers remain. - the new tap's hit-test path does not include the viewport or card subtree. the card's listener and ontap are not invoked. the new gesture arena contains only the scroll drag recognizer; the card's tap recognizer never joins it. subsequent taps are excluded from the card subtree during hit testing, so the cards' tap callbacks do not run. why scrolling still works while tapping does not from the flutter source, when a touch drag starts, scrollable creates a dragscrollactivity and uses ignorepointer to temporarily exclude the viewport subtree from hit testing. the scroll gesture recognizer sits outside that subtree and can still receive touch input. this explains how the list can continue scrolling while its cards cannot be tapped. the old pointers and hit-test paths in the device logs are consistent with a drag activity that never ends and a viewport that remains excluded from hit testing. however, we have not directly logged the dragscrollactivity or ignorepointer.ignoring state on the device. we used the same flutter card and scrolling components in a widget test to check this sequence: 1. a normal tap runs the callback, with ignoring=false. 2. send down/move for three pointers and deliberately omit up/cancel. the list scrolls, and ignoring=true. 3. send a complete down/up for a new pointer. the global pointer router receives the events, but the card callback does not run, and ignoring stays true. 4. send the missing up events for the three old pointers and wait for the drag to end. ignoring=false, and tapping the same card works again. this test verifies the flutter-side mechanism that causes tapping to remain disabled when terminal events are missing. it does not simulate the system screenshot service or identify the android function where the events are lost. we also replaced the same tab with a native compose page and checked another native tab. the screenshot gesture's terminal events likewise did not reach their touch views, but subsequent taps worked normally. missing terminal events were observed on both sides; persistent tap failure was reproduced only on the flutter page.
